article.story:
Barcelona restored their three-point lead at the top of LaLiga with a stunning second-half comeback against Villarreal at the Nou Camp.

Hansi Flick's looked on course for a second defeat of the campaign after a first period in which Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi put the visitors two goals up before Lamine Yamal crashed a penalty against the woodwork.

But the hosts moved up a gear after the interval, with three goals in 11 minutes turning the match on its head.

Gerard Martín pulled one back on 57 minutes and Fermín López restored parity four minutes later, before an own goal from Pau Navarro -- whose afternoon got worse when he was sent off in stoppage time -- completed the turnaround.

The visitors took a surprise lead in the fifth minute after Buchanan capitalised on Lopez sloppily giving the ball away and unleashed a 25-yard strike which beat Joan García.

Villarreal doubled their advantage two minutes later when Oluwaseyi latched onto a through ball in space and finished powerfully from a tight angle with his left foot into the roof of the net.

Barcelona had the chance to cut the deficit from the penalty spot after a VAR check showed goalscorer Oluwaseyi tripped Yamal inside the box, but the Spain star hit the post from 12 yards.

Yamal tried to make amends a couple of minutes later by cutting in and striking towards goal but his effort whistled narrowly wide.

The home side were starting to pin Villarreal back but were finding it hard to break through, Martin unable to guide his header on target from Yamal's free-kick and goalkeeper Péter Gulácsi then doing well to deny Eric García from inside the box.

Lopez was next to try his luck for Barcelona with an attempt from the edge of the box which looked destined for the bottom corner but Gulacsi got down well to push it away.

Barcelona's pressure finally told three minutes before the hour mark, when Martin flicked a header past Gulacsi from Pedri's cross.

They were on level terms four minutes later thanks to a perfectly executed counter-attack, Yamal cutting it back for Fermin who dispatched a left-footed shot into the bottom corner.

And the home fans did not have to wait long for the winner, Yamal's clever flick finding Garcia, whose cross was inadvertently poked into his own net by the unfortunate Navarro as he tried to clear.

Barcelona wanted more and Yamal was keen to get his name on the scoresheet too, but fired wide when he had space at the edge of the area.

Navarro's afternoon got worse in the third minute of added time when he was shown a second yellow card for bringing down Raphinha.
